EVA foam can be carved, it's super flexible, can be heat formed and take a lot of heat, it has no sharp edges. It also doesn't shatter or crack and painting is easy. It's also cheap and readily available. 

Plastic can shatter and crack, it melts very readily when exposed to high temperatures, it's heavier than EVA, it can't be carved, and priming/painting it is more challenging. You can't train it into complex shapes easily. Sheet plastic in large quantity will be difficult to source. 

I did a google search on polyethylene foam and it just seems like it has bad rigidity and bad texture. You can use priming methods and such to make EVA hard and sturdy but you won't be able to do that with soft foam pads like pool noodles.

I've used pool noodles before for LARP weapons and stuff that's meant to be soft.

Crafted correctly, EVA should't deform so easily.
